comment: The 10-Q does not disclose the up-to-$100bn OpenAI investment or a 10 GW letter of intent. It only discloses new SB Energy guarantees (capped at $105bn, ~4.25 GW of IT load) on behalf of an OpenAI affiliate, and 'equity investment commitments of $25 billion' in aggregate, neither of which is the $100bn OpenAI commitment.

The release gives no 'AI business' annual run rate figure at all. The closest disclosure is that Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the full fiscal year (growth of 43% for the quarter), which is a different measure from an AI business run rate, so no matching value can be reported.

The release discloses only the growth rate for Azure and other cloud services revenue (43%, 43% in constant currency) and the Intelligent Cloud segment total of $39.306bn; it does not give an Azure revenue dollar figure for the quarter, so the restated $29.417bn cannot be confirmed from this document. No supplemental Azure revenue table is included.
Document does not state the AI business annual run rate or 123% growth; Q4 FY2026 call has no update to that metric.
Document gives Q4 FY2026 weighted average RPO duration of 2.3 years, not the 2.5 years cited from the Jan 2026 call.
The January quote about GPUs being sold for the entire useful life does not appear in the Q4 FY2026 transcript.
Document gives June 2026 RPO and ex-OpenAI growth but no Dec 2025 ~45% OpenAI share, $625bn balance, 110%, or 28% rest growth.
Document does not disclose a change in server useful life from 6 to 5 years; it only says useful lives of equipment are reviewed on an ongoing basis.
Document does not present a construction in progress line or table; it discloses property and equipment, net by segment and total.

No AI revenue line is disclosed. AI is only described qualitatively as a driver within Google Cloud (enterprise AI Solutions / AI Infrastructure); no separate AI revenue figure appears anywhere in the release, so the 'no AI revenue line' claim still holds for Alphabet.

The 10-Q discloses no AI revenue line. Google Cloud revenues ($44.8bn for six months ended June 30, 2026) are described as including AI offerings, but they are cloud segment revenues, not an AI revenue figure, so the paper's 'no AI revenue line' claim stands for Alphabet.

No server/technical-infrastructure useful life is given. The closest disclosures are weighted-average remaining lease terms (operating leases 8.4 years, finance leases 8.6 years) and definite-lived intangible assets amortized over periods generally ranging from one to 10 years; neither is the server useful life the row describes.

Meta (the only company this document covers) still publishes no AI revenue line: revenue is disaggregated only into Advertising and Other revenue and into Family of Apps / Reality Labs. The paper's absence claim still holds for Meta.

No useful-life disclosure for servers/assets in this 10-Q; the only year figures given are lease terms (greater than one year to 30 years; 18-20 years). The paper's 'Meta: 5-5.5 years' cannot be confirmed from this document.
Document gives AI cloud bookings ('more than $30 billion of additional AI cloud contracts') but no AI revenue line. Oracle still does not publish an AI revenue figure.

Document does not state $75bn prepaid and customer-supplied hardware in AI deals. It reports customer prepayments with significant financing component for capital expenditures of $11.363bn in Q1 FY27 (and $4.592bn in Q4 FY26), not $75bn.

Oracle portion only. The 10-Q gives no AI revenue line; it reports cloud revenue of $11,607m and cloud infrastructure revenue of $7,388m, and RPO of $664bn, none of which is an AI-specific revenue figure, so the absence claim still holds for Oracle.
The 10-Q contains no covenant disclosure and no EBITDA/interest coverage ratio; the filing does not state the 3.0x test.
The 10-Q does not disclose a 6-year useful-life policy or figure for CoreWeave technology equipment; it only gives depreciation expense and lease terms.
The 10-Q gives a six-month increase in deferred revenue of $1,365 million, not an annual $2.7bn prepayment figure; annualizing would be computation.
The 10-Q does not disclose a CoreWeave financial covenant ratio or the number of tests; 3.0x is Oracle's covenant and is not in this document.
